item.title: Elder Nun Subhā: Here, people are lustful, Heedless, with defiled minds, They oppose each other as enemies, They struggle in disputes. Killing, binding, torturing, Losing…
item.description:
Elder Nun Subhā:

Here, people are lustful,
Heedless, with defiled minds,
They oppose each other as enemies,
They struggle in disputes.

Killing, binding, torturing,
Losing wealth, grieving, worrying —
Those who sink in sensual pleasures
Meet many calamities.

Why do my relatives,
Like my enemies,
Bind me into the circle of sensual pleasures?
Know that I have gone forth
Because I see that sensual pleasures are fearful.

Silver and gold cannot
Destroy the defilements.
Sensual pleasures are enemies,
Murderers, killers.
They are adversaries,
Darts, bonds.

Why do my relatives,
Like my enemies,
Bind me into the circle of sensual pleasures?
Know that I have gone forth —
Shaved my head, wearing the great robe.

Living on food
Accumulated by alms-round,
Robes made from discarded rags —
Living thus is suitable for me,
The basic life of homelessness.

Great sages have abandoned
Sensual desires, both divine and human.
Dwelling secure, liberated,
Unshaken, at ease.

Do not lead me to sensual desires —
There is no safety in sensual desires.
Sensual desires are enemies, murderers,
Producing suffering, like a heap of burning coals.

The path is dangerous, full of fear,
Full of suffering, with thorns —
The path of craving is rugged,
The path of delusion is vast.

Filled with terrifying calamities,
Sensual desires are like a snake’s head —
Fools delight in sensual desires,
Blind worldlings.

Beings sink in the muddy swamp —
Those who do not see the world,
They do not know
The end of birth and death.

People, because of sensual desires,
Go to evil destinations —
Most go that way,
Making themselves sick.

Thus, sensual desires produce enmity,
They burn, they defile.
Sensual desires belong to the body —
They bind people to death.

Sensual desires make one insane,
They cause disordered speech and mind,
They defile beings,
About to fall into Māra’s trap.

Sensual desires are endlessly perilous,
Full of suffering, a great poison —
Little sweetness, they create strife —
They wither the bright day.

Thus I decide —
I will not turn back because of sensual desires,
Which cause misfortune —
I will always delight in Nibbāna.

Fighting against sensual desires,
I wait, cool, calm —
I will live heedfully,
Destroying the fetters of sensual desire.

I follow that path
That the great sages have walked —
Sorrowless, stainless,
Safe, straight — the Eightfold Path.

See this Subhā,
Established in the true Dhamma —
A goldsmith’s daughter,
Attaining freedom from sensual desire,
Sitting in meditation,
At the root of a tree.

From: Therīgāthā 13.5

item.title: - “How, venerable sir, should one know, how should one see, so that ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises?” - “Monk, knowing and seeing…
item.description:
- “How, venerable sir, should one know, how should one see, so that ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises?” - “Monk, knowing and seeing the eye as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Knowing and seeing forms as impermanent … eye-consciousness … eye-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact … knowing and seeing that feeling as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … Knowing and seeing the mind as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Phenomena … mind-consciousness … mind-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact … knowing and seeing that feeling as impermanent, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises. Knowing thus, seeing thus, monks, ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge arises.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.53

item.title: The nun Vijayā, thinking “This is Māra,” recited this verse to Māra: Forms, sounds, tastes, smells, contacts — They delude the mind — I return…
item.description:
The nun Vijayā, thinking “This is Māra,” recited this verse to Māra:

Forms, sounds, tastes, smells, contacts —
They delude the mind —
I return them to you, Māra —
I have no need for them.
Regarding this impure body,
Easily broken and fragile,
I am humiliated and ashamed —
Craving for sensual desire is destroyed.
Those reborn in the form realm,
Those aspiring to the formless realm,
And those who attain peaceful concentration —
Everywhere, darkness is destroyed.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 5.4

item.title: “I do not see any other form, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a woman as the form of a man. The…
item.description:
“I do not see any other form, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a woman as the form of a man. The form of a man, monks, obsesses and occupies the mind of a woman.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.6

item.title: “Monks, thus I have opened the safe, secure path leading to happiness, closed the dangerous path, removed the male decoy, destroyed the female decoy. Monks,…
item.description:
“Monks, thus I have opened the safe, secure path leading to happiness, closed the dangerous path, removed the male decoy, destroyed the female decoy. Monks, whatever a teacher should do for his disciples out of compassion, that I have done for you out of compassion. Monks, here are the roots of trees, here are empty places. Meditate, do not be heedless, do not have cause for regret later. This is my instruction to you.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 19 – Dvedhāvitakkasutta

item.title: Elder Isidatta: “The five aggregates are fully understood, Standing with their root cut off. The destruction of suffering is attained, I have realized the destruction…
item.description:
Elder Isidatta:
“The five aggregates are fully understood,
Standing with their root cut off.
The destruction of suffering is attained,
I have realized the destruction of defilements.”

From: Theragāthā 1.120

item.title: - “Venerable Kaccāna, ‘guarding the sense faculties, guarding the sense faculties’ is said. To what extent, Venerable Kaccāna, is there guarding of the sense faculties?”…
item.description:
- “Venerable Kaccāna, ‘guarding the sense faculties, guarding the sense faculties’ is said. To what extent, Venerable Kaccāna, is there guarding of the sense faculties?” - “Here, brahmin, when a person sees a form with the eye, his mind inclines toward agreeable forms and recoils from disagreeable forms. He dwells with mindfulness unestablished, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Therefore, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are not abandoned without remainder. When he hears a sound … smells an odor … tastes a flavor … feels a touch … cognizes a phenomenon with the mind, his mind inclines toward agreeable phenomena and recoils from disagreeable phenomena. He dwells with mindfulness unestablished, with a limited mind. He does not know as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Therefore, evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are not abandoned without remainder. Thus, brahmin, there is non-guarding of the sense faculties.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.132

item.title: - “Friend, I do not abandon the present to chase after things subject to time. But, friend, I abandon things subject to time to chase…
item.description:
- “Friend, I do not abandon the present to chase after things subject to time. But, friend, I abandon things subject to time to chase after the present. The Blessed One has said that sensual pleasures are subject to time, of great suffering, of great despair — the peril in them is even greater. This Dhamma is visible here and now, not subject to time, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.20

item.title: “‘The ocean, the ocean,’ monks, an untaught ordinary person says. That, monks, is not the ocean in the noble one’s discipline. That is just a…
item.description:
“‘The ocean, the ocean,’ monks, an untaught ordinary person says. That, monks, is not the ocean in the noble one’s discipline. That is just a great mass of water, a great flood. Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. This, monks, is called the ocean in the noble one’s discipline. Here, this world with its devas, Māras, Brahmās, with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans, for the most part is submerged in it, tangled like a ball of thread, covered like a tangled skein, become like a tangled grass rope, unable to pass beyond the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower realm, saṃsāra.

Having destroyed ignorance, greed, and hatred,
This ocean with its many dangers —
With its sharks, crocodiles,
Whirlpools, and terrifying waves —
Is very hard to cross.

Having crossed the bond, escaped death,
Free from attachments,
Having made an end of suffering,
There is no further becoming.
He has destroyed birth and death,
The incomparable one —
I say that such a one
Has blinded Death.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.229

item.title: “Monks, these six sense bases — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained — bring suffering. What six? The eye sense base, monks — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained…
item.description:
“Monks, these six sense bases — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained — bring suffering. What six? The eye sense base, monks — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained — brings suffering. The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … The mind sense base, monks — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained — brings suffering. These six sense bases, monks — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained — bring suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.94
